submission.name: Trail Pantry
submission.tagline: Pack a better day trip with the food and supplies you already have.
submission.inspiration: Before a day hike or campus outing, it is easy to forget what snacks and supplies are already packed. We adapted a pantry helper idea for people planning short outdoor trips, where a quick inventory can make packing less stressful.
submission.what_it_does: Trail Pantry lets users photograph items, save them to a trip kit, and ask Gemini for simple snack or packing suggestions based on the list. It has a mobile-friendly inventory and a chat screen, though image scans sometimes miss items or label them incorrectly.
submission.how_we_built_it: We used Expo and React Native with TypeScript for the app, Firebase for sign-in and saved kits, and a FastAPI backend in Python. Google Cloud Vision identifies likely objects from a photo, then Gemini uses the saved list to suggest combinations and practical packing ideas. The app sends requests through the backend so keys stay off the client.
submission.challenges_we_ran_into: The scan results can be inconsistent, especially with cluttered photos, and the app occasionally shows a stale kit after saving. We also had to work through differences between browser and mobile behavior.
submission.accomplishments: We connected photo scanning, saved trip kits, and Gemini suggestions in a usable mobile flow. The main screens are in place, and a user can build and revisit a basic packing list.
submission.what_we_learned: We learned that a helpful AI suggestion depends on getting reliable inventory data first. We also got more practice tracing state and authentication issues across a mobile app and backend.
submission.whats_next: We would improve scan editing, add expiry and quantity fields, and make suggestions account for dietary needs and trip length.
